column1: # Generated by `lake exe oracle paths` (spec/Oracle.lean) from the definition
# in spec/Aontu: documents with paths, each case its declarations and a map
# as the schema against a map as the document, run in the default mode,
# without the fill (noFill) and under --partial (partial), as `verdict` rows
# whose expectation is the one class `vet` gives the document with its paths
# read as names, which `vetP_iff` makes the definition's own. A path resolves
# in the schema's own tree, through maps and lists and through nothing else,
# and reads as the term at its position in the schema met with the data; a
# path to nothing is an error, as is a document that reads only by its own
# paths. Regenerate with `make spec`; never edit by hand. The cases the ports
# do not yet answer this way are listed in spec/ledger.tsv.
# Paths through the riders follow in rows q0 on, which a path reads through,
# and key(n) reached through a path or a name, read where it lands, in rows r0 on.
# Relative paths, made absolute where each stands, follow in rows j0 on, with
# the bodies read at an alias's own place written again after the schema in
# maybe, absence where all that is wrong with a path is that it names nothing,
# in rows mb0 on, a list holding no position for absence in rows la0 on,
# and pref, each literal a preference and each preference a
# rank weaker, in rows pf0 on. Paths into a call's output, which resolve in the
# root with its calls made, follow in rows pc0 on, and move, a preference of
# the value a path reads with its source hidden, in rows mv0 on. Paths into
# what a call over a path makes, which resolve a round later, follow in rows
# rn0 on, and refer, a link that keeps its address, its template met into
# its target, in rows rf0 on. rel, a relation whose value holds a link at
# each leaf, follows in rows rl0 on, a constraint met with rel() before its
# value, which meets the value as any meet does, in rows rh0 on, and links
# read where they land, in a spread's template or copied by a path
# reference, in rows ld0 on, and in a generator's template, at each member
# of its output, in rows lg0 on. Spreads whose templates read their member's
# place, each read at each member there is, follow in rows sp0 on, and
# sources loaded in place, each a file of test/spec/files the definition
# declares as a term, in rows lf0 on.
# Generators whose templates read their member's place through a relative
# path, each read at each member of the output, follow in rows gt0 on, a
# filter's condition, read where the member it tries lands, in rows fc0 on,
# bounds written over terms, each the bound its terms name, in rows bd0 on, and
# bounds over a relative path in a generator's template or a filter's
# condition, each read where its instance lands, in rows bg0 on. Sources that
# declare names of their own, each read in its own scope, follow in rows ls0 on,
# and the names a source publishes, with the destructures that take them, in
# rows lx0 on. The transformer emit over a selection a path names follows in
# rows em0 on, and copy, its argument with the marks and the seal cleared at
# every depth, in rows cp0 on. Links whose templates read the member or the
# place where they land, each read there and only at the instances its own
# generator makes, follow in rows lt0 on. A call over a hole that a path names,
# which nothing binds, so the schema is an error whatever the data, in rows dp0 on.
# A meet carries the marks of both its sides, any's included, in rows hm0 on.
# A spread's template meets each member without the marks written around it
# (ruling 39), in rows sm0 on. A relative path in apply's template reads where
# the call stands, in rows ar0 on. A copy reads the relative paths it copies
# where it stands (ruling 26): a use of a name in rows cd0 on, written again
# after the schema in rows cdl0 on, a path reference in rows rc0 on, and a name
# whose body holds one, or a use inside a body read at the body's own place,
# in rows bc0 on, written again after the schema in rows bcl0 on. A name whose
# body holds a spread whose template reads its member's place reads it at each
# member where it's used and at its own place, in rows nt0 on and ntl0 on.
# A template in a selection's result reads its member's place where the
# selection stands, in rows st0 on and stl0 on.
# A path written in a disjunction's arm reads where the arm holds, in rows dj0
# on and djl0 on. A path inside a lone preference reads where the preference
# holds its value, and its parent arm lifts what the value reads as on its own
# (ruling 40), in rows lp0 on and lpl0 on.
